examples.question_text:
Find the volume of each solid in cm³.

a. A rectangular prism measures $5$ cm by $3$ cm by $8$ cm.

b. A cube has side length $4$ cm.
examples.solution_text:
a. The rectangular cross-section has area $5\times3$ cm².

$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=(5\times3)\times8\\&=120\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

b. The cube has a square cross-section and an equal distance through it.

$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=(4\times4)\times4\\&=64\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

The perpendicular sides are $12$ cm and $5$ cm. The $13$ cm slant side is not the triangle's height.

$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=\left(\frac{12\times5}{2}\right)\times8\\&=30\times8\\&=240\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

Use the perpendicular height of the parallelogram.

$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=(8\times4)\times9\\&=32\times9\\&=288\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

The uniform cross-section is the trapezium-shaped side wall. Its parallel sides are the two depths, and the perpendicular distance between them is $18.6$ m. The distance through the prism is the pool's width.

$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{18.6(1.35+2.75)}{2}\\&=38.13\text{ m}^{2}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=38.13\times6.4\\&=244.032\text{ m}^{3}\\&\approx244.03\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A school makes $40$ identical doorstops from recycled plastic. Each doorstop is a triangular prism with a right-triangle cross-section of base $6$ cm and perpendicular height $2$ cm. Each prism is $4$ cm long. Find the total volume of plastic needed in cm³.
examples.solution_text:
For one doorstop:

$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=\left(\frac{6\times2}{2}\right)\times4\\&=6\times4\\&=24\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

For all $40$ doorstops:

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{total}}&=40\times24\\&=960\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Two rectangular prisms have the same volume. Prism A measures $5$ cm by $4$ cm by $x$ cm. Prism B measures $8$ cm by $6$ cm by $5$ cm. Find $x$.
examples.solution_text:
For prism B:

$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=(8\times6)\times5\\&=240\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

Prism A has the same volume.

$\begin{aligned}(5\times4)x&=240\\20x&=240\\x&=240\div20\\x&=12\end{aligned}$

The missing length is $12$ cm.

examples.question_text: A prism has a uniform cross-sectional area of $28$ cm² and a volume of $1540$ cm³. Find its length in cm.
A vase occupies $260$ cm³ inside a rectangular box with internal dimensions of $11$ cm by $8$ cm by $7$ cm. Packing foam fills the remaining space. Find the volume of foam in cm³.
examples.solution_text:
For the box:

$\begin{aligned}V&=Ah\\&=(11\times8)\times7\\&=616\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

Subtract the volume occupied by the vase.

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{foam}}&=616-260\\&=356\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

coverage.summary: Authored eight worked examples covering all distinct retained assessment methods, including cube volume, perpendicular-height selection, contextual cross-section orientation, repeated objects, missing dimensions, equal volumes and packing space. Used different values and the supplied booklet's methods. Separate editable question and solution fields use single-dollar mathematics, aligned relation signs and renderer-inherited blue solution prose/math. Useful planar cross-section diagrams have black ink, unshaded interiors and explicit 10 pt labels. No existing examples were supplied. Assessments were classified only; their mathematics was neither altered nor re-audited. Independent example review and actual rendered visual verification remain pending.

examples.derivation: Rectangle: A=5×3=15 cm², V=15×8=120 cm³. Cube: A=4×4=16 cm², V=16×4=64 cm³.
The marked perpendicular sides are 12 cm and 5 cm; their hypotenuse is 13 cm. A=12×5÷2=30 cm², so V=30×8=240 cm³.
The dashed height meets the base perpendicularly. A=8×4=32 m², so V=32×9=288 m³.
The parallel depths are 1.35 m and 2.75 m, separated by 18.6 m. A=18.6×4.10÷2=38.13 m². V=38.13×6.4=244.032 m³, rounding to 244.03 m³.
One doorstop has A=6×2÷2=6 cm² and V=6×4=24 cm³. Forty require 40×24=960 cm³.
Prism B has volume 8×6×5=240 cm³. Equal volumes give 20x=240, hence x=12 and the missing length is 12 cm.
The internal box volume is 11×8×7=616 cm³. Foam occupies 616−260=356 cm³.

review.summary: All eight examples pass independent mathematical, source, method and scope review. All 31 exact assessment locators are mapped, and the eight distinct methods have example coverage. No existing examples were supplied. Working has appropriate relation-sign alignment; no bare expression requires a phantom equals gutter. Solutions retain editable prose and inherit blue styling. The diagrams contain givens only, use black ink and specify 10 pt labels. No additional syllabus exception is required. Accepted assessments were classified without repeating their mathematical audit. Actual rendering and final-size label verification remain for the later visual stage.
